decision: Bind each calibrated topology selection result to a canonical SHA-256 digest of the exact calibration report set used for evaluation.

reviews.correctness: Preferred an explicit evidence-set digest because topology IDs and Git SHA alone do not prove which measured RAM/CPU/probe-latency values produced the winner.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred canonical offline hashing over mutable filenames or caller-provided labels; report order is normalized and any evidence-field change changes the digest.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred local SHA-256 over an external evidence store or signing service: zero qrexec round trips, negligible CPU/memory, and no MissionQueue/coordinator semantic changes.

alternatives_rejected: Topology IDs + Git SHA only: insufficient evidence identity; measured values can be swapped while identifiers remain unchanged.
Persist reports to filenames and return paths: paths are not content identity and can be replaced.
External attestation/evidence database: stronger auditability later, but adds service lifecycle, credentials, latency, and failure modes before real Qubes qualification exists.
qa: Digest is independent of report ordering.
Changing measured report evidence changes the digest.
Operational command returns schemaVersion 2 and the digest alongside the winner.
Candidate/config provenance validation still occurs before any synthetic workload starts.
failure_lessons: A winner bound only to topology IDs and commit SHA is not bound to the exact measurement set that justified it.
Canonicalization is required before hashing because object key/report ordering must not create false digest differences.
